note.question: How can improved data sharing and daily route optimization support redesigning sample transportation in malawi?
note.overview: Healthcare systems in resource-limited settings rely on diagnostic networks in which medical samples (e.g., blood, sputum) and results need to be transported between geographically dispersed healthcare facilities and centralized laboratories. Existing sample transportation (ST) systems typically operate fixed schedules, which do not account for demand variability and lead to unnecessary transportation visits as well as delays. The paper's solution approach performs well in a range of numerical experiments.

source.quote: Problem definition: Healthcare systems in resource-limited settings rely on diagnostic networks in which medical samples (e.g., blood, sputum) and results need to be transported between geographically dispersed healthcare facilities and centralized laboratories.

Based on analysis of field data describing over 20,000 samples and results transported during July–October 2019, we show that the implementation of OST routes reduced average ST delays in three districts of Malawi by approximately 25%.

Whereas the MDP version of the problem is generally intractable due to the size of the state space required to capture each of the different stages in the ST network, the formulation is useful, as it allows us to develop a lower bound on the optimal solution (for small networks) (see Section A2.2 in the e-companion).
